articleTitle: A Spatio-Temporal Associative Memory Architecture Using Chaotic Masking Technique for Complex Sequence Storage and Retrieval
abstract: A spatio-temporal associative memory neural network architecture based on hetero-associative memory neural network and chaotic masking techniques is proposed. By using chaotic masking techniques for preprocessing and multiple hetero-associative memory neural networks, the process of complex sequences avoids many problems like confusion and gets easier. The experiments show that this architecture is capable of storing and retrieving complex spatio-temporal patterns, where some spatial patterns are highly-correlated and even repetitive while other related works can not do.

articleTitle: Emotion-Driven Memcapacitor Biomimetic Circuit for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Most of the previous operational conditioned reflex neural network circuits were built using traditional memristors. With the discovery of the memcapacitors, memcapacitors offer greater advantages than memristors in simulating neural biological behaviors for reinforcement learning. A reinforcement learning neural network circuit based on memcapacitors is proposed in this paper. Within this framework, reinforcement learning and forgetting of operant conditioning are successfully implemented. Additionally, the internal states involved in emotion generation and regulation that influence decision-making have been simulated. This work provides an implementation idea for the hardware implementation of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Personalized Federated Learning with Multi-Server
abstract: In recent years, multi-server federated learning has gained significant attention in cross-device scenarios due to its capability to reduce communication delay. Classic multi-server federated learning algorithms simply use clients located in overlapping service areas to aggregate the model parameters from regional servers they can access, which ultimately train a common global model. However, the global model obtained through this approach often exhibit poor generalization performance on heterogeneous data. To overcome this challenge, we propose personalized federated learning based on adaptive model fusion (pFedAF). This method employs a Local Pre-aggregation (LP) module to adaptively aggregate the local models of clients with regional models, ultimately generating personalized models suited to the clients' private data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed pFedAF can effectively improve model performance on non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data. Compared to other multi-server federated learning algorithms, our pFedAF algorithm demonstrates superior performance in Non-IID scenarios.

articleTitle: Capacity Optimization Configuration of Wind-Solar Hydrogen Production Hybrid Energy Storage System
abstract: Wind-solar-hydrogen production offers an effective solution to both power curtailment and green hydrogen production challenges. The capacity configuration of a wind-solar-hydrogen storage system plays a crucial role in optimizing its economic operation. To address this, a wind-solar-hydrogen storage energy system was developed. Initially, a density-based clustering algorithm with noise handling and an ordered clustering algorithm were employed to classify a year's worth of wind, solar output, and electrical load data into three representative days. The system's capacity optimization was then performed with the objective of maximizing the net system revenue for each device. A comparison was made with the traditional approach of minimizing the net present value of costs. The results revealed that maximizing net project revenue as the objective function leads to superior economic outcomes, outperforming the cost-minimization approach and resulting in a more optimized system configuration.

articleTitle: Multi-Strategy Collaborative Improved Seagull Optimization Algorithm and Its Applications
abstract: In this paper, in order to improve the search ability and adaptability of the seagull optimization algorithm, a multi-strategy collaborative improvement-based seagull optimization algorithm (MI-SOA) is proposed. Firstly, LogisticsTent chaotic mapping with is introduced to enhance the global search ability of the algorithm; secondly, the algorithm's search path is optimized by filtering out the superior and inferior solution locations through the inverse learning strategy to improve the quality of the solution; the algorithm combines the Lévy flights and the positive cosine operator, which enhances the algorithm's local search accuracy and flexibility; the improved seagull optimization algorithm has been developed in the mathematical model and parameter settings are optimized, and by adjusting the iterative process and parameter selection of the algorithm, the algorithm can be better adapted to various complex optimization problems. The experimental results show that the MI-SOA algorithm has better performance and faster optimization ability than other algorithms in solving numerical optimization problems; the improved seagull optimization algorithm is applied to three-dimensional path planning problems in practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Output Synchronization of Multi-Layer Networks with Output Coupling Under Dynamic Event-Triggered Control
abstract: The article discusses the output synchronization (OS) of multi-layer networks (MLNs) based on output coupling (OC). By exploiting graph theory and Lyapunov function, sufficient conditions for OS of MLNs under dynamic event-triggered control (DETC) are derived, and Zeno behavior is excluded. Unlike the previous case, the coupling of OS targets in different layers of networks is considered in this article. Ultimately, a numerical simulation validates the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Emolip: An Affective Computing Way Based on Image-Language Pre-Trained Model
abstract: This paper presents Emolip, an effective emotion recognition way based on Image-Language Pre-trained Model, designed to reduce costs and computational complexity. Emolip leverages a Image-Language Pre-training approach. The model utilizes a linear attention mechanism to enhance efficiency, outperforming traditional methods by reducing computational time. The experimental results, based on the EMOTIC dataset, demonstrate a significant improvement in recognition speed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Prescribed Group Consensus of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Networks Based on Merging Mechanism, Hierarchical Architecture, and Impulsive Control
abstract: This paper mainly studies the dynamic prescribed group consensus of nonlinear multi-agent networks. Firstly, a merging mechanism is introduced to simulate dynamic merging of different agent groups into the network. Secondly, a hierarchical architecture is adopted to lay the foundation for the establishment of multi-agent network dynamics, and the hierarchical architecture includes virtual layer and real layer, which has the advantages of high practicality. Thirdly, a impulsive control protocol is designed to achieve the dynamic prescribed group consensus control of multi-agent networks, which has the advantage of high efficiency. Finally, the practicality and efficiency of the proposed theories are verified through a series of simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Fixed/Predefined Time Intra-Layer Synchronization in Multi-Layer Networks*
abstract: This study is dedicated to probing into novel methodologies for attaining predefined-time intra-layer synchronization within multi-layer complex networks. Using particular functions, relatively less stringent conditions are furnished for the predefined time synchronization control strategy. Concurrently, a more accurate estimation of the stabilization time is obtained. Moreover, a specific exploration of synchronization strategies based on the predefined-time approach is carried out. This empowers the synchronization duration to be predetermined in line with practical requisites, independent of system parameters and initial conditions. Eventually, the efficacy of the proposed approach is verified by numerical simulations, thereby proffering novel theoretical foundations and practical guidelines for synchronization management in multi-layer networks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Low-Rank Adaptation Based Parameter-Efficient Tuning for Low-Resource Zero-Shot Remote Sensing Image Classification
abstract: Zero-shot remote sensing image classification is a technique that enables models to predict on unseen categories, effectively addressing the challenges associated with the dynamic changes in surface types typical of remote sensing images and the high costs of acquiring extensive labeled data. Currently, shallow neural network algorithms are widely applied in this field However, these algorithms have certain limitations in capturing the complex spatial relationships of land objects. In this study, we transfer the multimodal CLIP model to the remote sensing field, utilizing its advanced training mechanisms to significantly enhance the ability to handle zero-shot tasks in remote sensing image classification by learning the semantic associations between images and text. However, the parameter size of CLIP reaches 151.28M, which brings significant computational costs and limits its practical application in the remote sensing domain. To address these issues, we innovatively introduce AdaLoRA, an efficient parameter fine-tuning strategy designed to reduce the trainable parameter volume and training duration of pre-trained models. This strategy not only maintains the model's classification ability for zero-shot tasks but also makes it more suitable for the specific needs of the remote sensing field. Therefore, in our research, weapply the AdaLoRA strategy to the CLIP model and conduct experiments on the PatternNet, NWPU-RESISC45, and EuroSAT datasets. The results demonstrate that our approach achieves highermodel performance while reducing training time compared to state-of-the-art models.

Author Keywords: Zero-shot remote sensing image classification CLIP

articleTitle: A Greenhouse Tomato Irrigation System Based on Fuzzy PID Control
abstract: Soil moisture management during the critical growth stages of greenhouse tomatoes has a decisive impact on fruit size, set, and yield. Traditional Proportional-Integral-Derivative control lacks the flexibility and adaptability required for precise irrigation. To solve the above-mentioned problem, this paper puts forward an intelligent irrigation system grounded on a PID control strategy enhanced by fuzzy logic, integrating Internet of Things technology in greenhouse tomatoes. Experimental comparisons were conducted between the fuzzy PID control algorithm and the PID control algorithm. The findings show that the fuzzy PID control outperforms in aspects of accuracy, stability, and adaptability. The designed intelligent irrigation system features low cost, high automation, and precise soil moisture control, thereby enhancing tomato yield and quality, while significantly conserving water resources.

articleTitle: Neuroscience-Inspired Neural Network Exhibits More Human-Like Face Processing Abilities
abstract: This study introduces an updated version of AlexNet called Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE)-AlexNet inspired by neuroscience findings. We compared SE-AlexNet's performance with the original AlexNet and VGG16 models (for object-based and face-based ones), focusing on their ability to imitate human face processing. Using an adapted behavioral experimental method, we assessed the models' perceptual sensitivity and accuracy in face perception. SE-AlexNet, especially with a 16-fold compression ratio, outperformed the other models, closely matching human performance in recognizing facial emotions. These results suggest that a neuroscience-inspired CNN model can replicate human-like perception in specific computer vision tasks rather than more complicated models.

articleTitle: Weed Recognition Method Based on a Lightweight YOLOv5
abstract: Weeds, as one of the important hazards that interfere with crop growth in the production process, cause huge economic losses every year. To achieve the development of smart agriculture, solving the problem of weeds plays a key role in improving crop health and increasing yields. This article focuses on identifying common weeds in farmland and automatically recognizes them by introducing the YOLOv5 model. Based on practical application scenarios, the model has decided to replace the feature extraction network with GhostNet and make lightweight improvements to reduce the computational complexity of model parameters; And introduce the CA attention mechanism module to further enhance the ability to extract location information of detection targets and improve detection accuracy. The experimental results show that the proposed model reduces the number of parameters by 24%, floating-point operations by 32%, model size by 3.2M, and mAP by 0.8% compared to the original model.

articleTitle: Integrated Wavelet Decomposition and Multi-Model Approach with Fractional-Order Sparrow Search Optimization for ECG Classification
abstract: The classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals plays a crucial role in medical diagnostics, as accurate classification can significantly enhance the efficiency of heart disease diagnosis. This research introduces a novel method, Integrated Wavelet Decomposition and Multi-Model Approach with Fractional-Order Sparrow Search Optimization (WMFO). The method employs wavelet decomposition (WD) to decompose ECG signals into six distinct frequency components, with each component being trained using different models. The hyperparameters of these models are fine-tuned through the Fractional-Order Sparrow Search Algorithm (FOSSA), further improving the adaptability and accuracy of the models. The WMFO achieved a balanced accuracy of 93.08%, a geometric mean of 82.87%, and a Youden's index of 80.27% on the MIT-BIH arrhythmia dataset. Additionally, ablation and comparative experiments demonstrated the superior performance of this method in ECG classification tasks.

Author Keywords: Wavelet Decomposition and Multi-Model Approach with Fractional-Order Sparrow Search Optimization

articleTitle: EV Load Forecasting Method Based on Data Reconstruction of GRU-WGAN and BiLSTM Network
abstract: With the popularity of electric vehicles, proper prediction of the charging load of electric vehicles is of great importance in order to ensure the reliable functioning of the electrical grid. However, EV load data will inevitably have missing and abnormal problems during the collection and transmission process, which hinders the improvement of load forecasting accuracy. In this paper, we propose a load forecasting approach based on GRU-WGA-BiLSTM. First, modelling of timing data using gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks to capture the complex dependencies in the charging load data. We employ the GAN to reconstruct the dataset. Then, we utilize the adversarial training mechanism to enhance both the authenticity and quality of the reconstructed data. we apply the Generative Adversarial Network to reconstruct the data and use the adversarial training mechanism to improve the authenticity and quality of the reconstructed data. The reconstructed data is used as input to the BiLSTM network for predicting the charging load. Experimental findings show that the proposed model is superior in handling missing data and predicting load. In comparison to conventional interpolation techniques and forecasting models, the data integrity and prediction accuracy are significantly improved.

articleTitle: Cooperative Output Regulation of Heterogeneous Fractional-order Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: In this paper, the cooperative output regulation is addressed for a sort of heterogeneous fractional-order multi-agent systems. Firstly, to identify the state of the exosystem, a distributed dynamic observer is designed. Secondly, two types of distributed fractional control schemes are developed separately based on the states and outputs of agents to solve cooperative output regulation. Some concise criteria are further derived by virtue of the stability result of fractional linear models. To demonstrate the validity of the derivation of the results, a specific numerical example is also given.

articleTitle: Violence Detection Using EfficientNet-B0 and SA-Separable Convolutional LSTM
abstract: Automatic detection of violent behavior is an important research task in the construction of modern smart cities. To address this huge challenge, we proposed a deep learning model that combines the lightweight network EfficientNet-B0 and the deep separable convolutional long short-term memory (SepConvolutional LSTM) network. The model adopted a background subtraction algorithm to reduce the model's computational cost. Finally, the model integrated the self-attention mechanism into the deep separable convolutional LSTM module, thereby enhancing the model's ability to capture key information in videos. The model was applied on the largest violent dataset and its effectiveness was evaluated. The final results show that our model has superior performance in terms of computational complexity and accuracy.

articleTitle: Apple Grade Classification Based on Convolutional Neural Network and Machine Learning
abstract: The classification of apple grades is crucial for apple sales. Using computer vision technology as a non-destructive method to classify fruits has the advantages of high speed, applicability and high precision. This study focuses on the classification of apple grades using convolutional neural networks (CNN) and machine learning (ML) models. Firstly, the transfer learning method is adopted, and six popular CNN architectures (VGG-16, VGG-19, ResNet-50, MobileNet, EfficientNet, and Inception_V3) are used to compare the effects of different convolutional neural network models in processing apple classification. The results show that EfficientNet has the highest classification accuracy. Secondly, combining CNN and ML model, using EfficientNet to extract depth features and training ML models: K nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest classifier (RFC) and support vector machine (SVM) respectively. The results show that the classification accuracy is improved. Finally, the ensemble learning method is used to integrate multiple CNN_ML models through voting mechanism, and the final classification model is obtained, with an accuracy rate of 98.21%. According to the experimental results, this study was successful in apple grade classification and provided new ideas for apple grade classification.

articleTitle: Memristor-Based Neural Network Circuit of Emotional Grading in Intelligence Decision System
abstract: Emotion is a crucial factor in neuromorphic computing. Current memristive circuits have explored the impact of emotion on operant conditioning, there is a lack of behavioral research on emotional decision-making. This paper proposes a memristor-based neural network circuit of emotional grading in intelligence decision system, which mainly includes emotion generation module, emotion grading module, emotion monitoring module and intelligent decision-making module. This circuit can convert external stimulus signals into emotional signals and classify the emotional signals for processing. The graded emotional signals are used to make decisions through a memristive neural network, and ultimately output the behavior after the decision. The emotional intensity will also be monitored in real-time to ensure that it is within the normal range. The simulation results are validated by PSPICE, providing a reference for artificial intelligence and brain like computing.

articleTitle: Asynchronous Iterative Q-Learning: Optimal Control for Nonlinear Discrete-Time Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel asynchronous iterative Q-learning algorithm (AIQL) to solve the optimal control problem for nonlinear discrete-time systems. AIQL utilizes two Q-value functions, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q}_{i}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q}_{i-n}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q}_{i}$</tex> is used for improving the control policy, while <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q}_{i-n}$</tex> is used to evaluate the policy's performance. The advantage of this structure is that it decouples policy evaluation from policy improvement, thus reducing estimation bias. Additionally, the paper provides a convergence proof for AIQL, showing that both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q}_{i}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q}_{i-n}$</tex> converge to the optimal solution. Neural networks based on the actor-critic framework are employed to implement asynchronous iterative Q-learning. Simulation results demonstrate that asynchronous iterative Q-learning outperforms the traditional iterative Q-learning (IQL) algorithm, particularly in terms of reducing estimation bias and achieving better control performance.

articleTitle: Neural Network SLAM Algorithms for Dynamic Object Removal in Complex Environments
abstract: To address the issues of accuracy degradation or even operational failure of simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms in dynamic, complex, and low-texture environments, this paper proposes a target detection and dynamic point cloud removal algorithm based on a lightweight neural network. This algorithm integrates visual feature extraction with moving object detection to reduce the interference of dynamic targets in localization. A plane-matching technique is employed to overcome the lack of features in low-texture environments. Additionally, dynamic object 3D point clouds are removed using 3D data generated by laser scanning. On the KITTI dataset, the algorithm achieves a 53.59% reduction in root mean square error (RMSE) of absolute trajectory compared to the DynaSLAM algorithm, with significant improvement in dynamic point cloud removal accuracy. Results demonstrate the proposed algorithm's excellent localization accuracy, operational efficiency, and robustness.

articleTitle: DiffPPO: Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models for Text-to-Image Generation
abstract: In recent years, significant progress has been made in the field of text-to-image generation, particularly with the application of diffusion models. However, existing diffusion models still face challenges in accurately understanding complex textual inputs, precisely controlling object attributes and quantities in the generated images, and maintaining consistency within the scene. To address the limitations of existing diffusion models in generating high-quality images that align with textual prompts, we propose a method called DiffPPO. This approach fine-tunes the diffusion model using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm and models the denoising process as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). We introduce an Actor-Critic architecture with a value network to reduce the variance of the policy gradient. Additionally, we employ dynamically adjusted KL divergence regularization and entropy regularization to balance the exploration of the image generation policy with the consistency of the pretrained model. Experimental results show that DiffPPO outperforms traditional supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning methods in generating images with complex attributes such as shape, emotion, quantity, and artistic style, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Detection of Power Transmission Lines Using an Improved RT-DETR Model
abstract: The stability of power energy systems is paramount for both societal productivity and the well-being of individuals. Despite being the prevailing real-time object detection frame-work, the YOLO series detectors have demonstrated respectable performance in such applications. However, due to the existence of post-processing Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS), they fall short of achieving true end-to-end detection. Similarly, DETR-type detectors are rarely utilized for real-time object detection due to their prohibitive computational costs until the introduction of RT-DETR. This paper introduces multiple plug-and-play modules aimed at addressing three key aspects (spatial redundancy, channel information loss, and insufficient multiscale feature fusion) to refine the Neck layer of the original RT-DETR model, thereby significantly enhancing its performance. Moreover, accurate electrical system detection requires heightened precision, particularly under high Intersection Over Union (IOU) thresholds, leading to the adoption of different matching cost computation methods at various training stages to shift the model's attention from local to global. Finally, on our in-house dataset demonstrates an approximately 2% improvement in mean average precision (MAP) compared to the original RT-DETR, consistently surpassing prevalent real-time object detectors and affirming the effectiveness of the proposed enhancement strategy in electrical system detection. Despite the considerable drop in Frames Per Second (FPS) due to the introduction of multiple modules, the inference speed is still comparable to that of some real-time object detectors, which we find acceptable.

articleTitle: Estimating the Domain of Attraction in Saturated Constrained Linear Discrete-Time Impulsive Systems Based on an Improved Convex Hull Representation
abstract: This paper explores methods that utilize an enhanced convex hull representation and composite quadratic Lyapunov functions to increase the estimation of the domain of attraction for linear discrete impulsive systems with actuator saturation. The primary objectives are to derive stability conditions using the improved convex hull representation and to develop strategies for estimating the domain of attraction internally by constructing composite quadratic Lyapunov functions. Several examples are provided to validate the effectiveness of the pronosed conditions.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Social Power Evolution in Cooperation Networks Based on the Interval Reflected Appraisals
abstract: This paper proposes a mathematical model based on interval reflective evaluation to investigate the evolution of social power within cooperative networks. On a single time scale, opinion dynamics adhere to the Friedkin-Johnsen (F-J) model, incorporating iterative self-weighting updates. By employing matrix vectorization, the system is reformulated into a nonlinear mapping. Then, the Banach Fixed Point Theorem substantiates the existence of an equilibrium point, while its uniqueness and convergence depend on individual susceptibility. Some numerical simulations validate the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Community Energy Management System Based on Deep Learning and Lagrangian Programming Neural Network
abstract: In this paper, a innovative approach is proposed for solving the energy scheduling problem (ESP) in community energy management system (CEMS), combining deep learning with lagrangian programming neural network (LPNN). First, The LPNN is employed to address the ESP, and its effectiveness is thereafter validated. Subsequently, a deep learning-based LPNN (DLPNN) model accompanied by a specially designed loss function is introduced. This enables the trained DLPNN to solve the ESP in CEMS without the need for repeated steps, which is a limitation of using LPNN alone. Additionally, the dynamic variables in the ESP are incorporated as input variables for training the DLPNN, allowing the model to determine optimal solutions for varying values of these variables. Ultimately, the effectiveness of the introduced approach is confirmed through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Scheduling Gain-Based Adaptive NN Control of Underactuated Bridge Crane
abstract: Bridge crane is an important industrial device, and is widely applied to many fields such as automobile making and marine equipment. However, the existing control methods have encountered some challenges in the applications owing to the underactuation, strong nonlinearity and external disturbance. This work proposes an adaptive control scheme for the underactuated bridge crane with uncertainties. The non-strict feedback structure is simplified a strict-feedback one by employing the property of neural networks (NNs). Moreover, the computation complexity is reduced by virtue of the approximation ability of NNs. A scheduling gain and a robust item are added to the control input to improve the robustness of algorithm. The unknown control direction problem is tackled by using the adaptive control technique. Further, a scheduling gain-based adaptive control method is proposed by consisting of the NNs and the adaption law to ensure all signals are bounded. The simulation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of an Adversarial Training Defense Algorithm for Network Traffic
abstract: At present, there are more and more attacks targeting network traffic, among which adversarial sample attack method is a popular attack method in recent years, which brings relatively high Security threats. This paper studies the basic principles of network traffic adversarial attacks and adversarial defense, designs a network traffic defense algorithm based on adversarial training to resist adversarial attacks, and verifies its effectiveness and accuracy on the ISCXVPN-2016 dataset.

articleTitle: An External Knowledge-Based Sentiment Classification Method for Chinese Short Texts
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet applications, a large number of short texts expressing public opinion with emotional views have been generated. The subtexts of these short texts are complex, which bring a great challenge to emotional classification. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a method for sentiment classification of Chinese short texts based on fused external knowledge. Firstly, we construct a prompt text with fused sentiment knowledge, splice the prompt text with the original input text into the pre-training language model, and guide the pre-training model through the prompt. Then, we design label words for the text domain and map the prediction results for classification. The experimental results show that this method exhibits good performance on the Meituan Waimai dataset, with an accuracy of 81.3%, which are 1.8%, 2.2% and 3.5% higher than the mainstream modeling methods such as BERT, TextCNN and ERINE, respectively.

articleTitle: Event-Based Prescribed-Time Adaptive Neural Network Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the event-triggered (ET) practical prescribed-time (PPT) adaptive neural network control design problem for uncertain nonlinear systems. Neural networks technology is used to deal with unknown nonlinear functions in nonlinear systems. Unlike traditional command filtering control approaches, a novel PPT error compensation mechanism is introduced to precisely regulate the settling time of filtering errors, rather than the upper bound of the convergence time after scaling, thereby effectively reducing the impact of filtering errors. Meanwhile, an ET mechanism utilizing the switching threshold strategy is designed to reduce the high update frequency and enhance the control efficiency. It can be proved that all signals in nonlinear systems meet the PPT stability requirement. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is demonstrated through a numerical example.

articleTitle: Self-Triggered Impulsive Control for Quasi-Synchronization of Nonlinear Systems with Application to Neural Networks
abstract: This paper addresses the quasi-synchronization problem in nonlinear systems by introducing a novel self-triggered impulsive control(STIC) strategy. Firstly, a new self-triggered control(STC) mechanism is proposed to establish the relationship between consecutive impulsive instants, allowing the timing of the next impulse to be predicted based on the previous one. Secondly, sufficient conditions for achieving quasi-synchronization are derived using a comparative system approach. Finally, the proposed design scheme is applied to the quasi-synchronization of neural networks(NNs). The STIC strategy presented in this paper eliminates the need for real-time state monitoring, significantly reducing communication costs and improving resource efficiency. A numerical example is provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Context Understanding in Real Time Video Analysis Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for context understanding in real-time video analysis. With the proliferation of video data across various domains, effective context interpretation is crucial for applications such as surveillance, autonomous driving, and interactive systems. We present a novel framework that leverages CNNs to extract spatial and temporal features from video streams, enabling enhanced recognition of complex scenes and interactions. Our experiments demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and processing speed compared to traditional methods. We also discuss the implications of our findings for future research in video analysis and intelligent systems.

articleTitle: Region Attractivity Analysis for Multi-Modality Data Driven Recurrent Neural Networks
abstract: The multi-modalilty artificial intelligence is the hot research topic. However the existing neural networks (NNs) stability results are only related to constant or periodic inputs. The multi-modality artificial intelligence requires that neural networks must be able to cope with modality signals, i.e., including constant, periodic and aperiodic signals at the same time. Hence, this paper presents sufficient conditions for region attractivity of neural networks driven by modality data, i.e., hybrid external inputs. By using the comparison method and construting the Lyapunov fuctions, global attractivity conditions are given for NNs driven by multimodality data. For verifying the derived results, two three dimensional NN are simulated.

articleTitle: Decentralized Online Dual Averaging Optimization Ensuring Differential Privacy and Expected Regret
abstract: The decentralized storage feature of big data may potentially expose risks of privacy breaches during real-time information interactions. To address this concern, this study focuses on constrained online learning problems with privacy awareness over generally directed communication networks. Specifically, we develop a novel secure decentralized online algorithm that utilizes the idea of the dual-averaging method as a core dynamic procedure. Different from existing dual-averaging works, the proposed algorithm admits arbitrary initial conditions, which is more flexible and generalized. The algorithm performs a gradient scaling operation on the dual dynamics, which effectively eliminates errors caused by unbalanced communications. The results show that the proposed algorithm ensures both differential privacy and expected regret. Simulations further confirm the correctness of our work.

articleTitle: Mixture Random Features Spaces for Robust Adaptive Filtering
abstract: Kernel adaptive filters (KAFs) based on random features spaces, e.g., random Fourier features space (RFFS) and Gaussian Hermite Fourier space (GHFS) have obtained significant success in signal processing. However, RFFS and GHFS face challenges of insufficient approximation accuracy and performance sensitivity to input dimensionality, respectively. To address these issues, a novel mixture random features spaces (MRFS) method is proposed based on multikernel method. Combining the maximum correntropy criterion (MCC) and stochastic gradient method, a robust mixture random features spaces maximum correntropy criterion (MRFSMCC) algorithm is thus obtained. Simulations on nonlinear system identification and Mackey-Glass time-series prediction validate the superiorities of proposed MRFSMCC under mixed impulsive environments.

articleTitle: Tibetan Syllable Component Recognization with Memristor
abstract: This paper highlights a Tibetan syllable component recognization method by using memristors. Firstly, a memristor crossbar array with an external control circuit is designed to present both elevated device density and the potential for parallel computing. Then a syllable component recognization method is implemented to classify syllable into seven types, prefix letter, root letter, superscript letter, subscript letter, vowel letter, suffix letter, and farther suffix letter, matching Tibetan characters by computing total current value in memristor crossbar array. Finally, Tibetan characters is re-encoded in binary according to the last two digits of their Unicode, and input by controlling the voltage in memristor crossbar array. Experiments demonstrate that our method recognizes general Tibetan syllable components.

articleTitle: Anti-Windup Approach for Time-Delay Saturated Impulsive Control System
abstract: An anti-windup compensator with input time-delay is designed for impulsive system under input saturation constraint here. Some exponential stability criteria are derived based on matrix inequalities and algebraic inequalities. An anti-windup gain is proposed to guarantee the maximum attraction domain. An example is utilized to show the validity of the delayed anti-windup compensator.

articleTitle: MamAM: A Novel Deep Reinforcement Learning Architecture for Multi-Robot Task Allocation
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for efficiently solving multi-robot task allocation(MRTA) problems, which include tasks characterized by deadlines and workload, as well as constraints related to the robots' working capacity.We propose a method called the Mamba Attention Model (MamAM), which consists of two main components: an encoder and a decoder. The encoder, based on the Mamba Network, is responsible for capturing the global dependencies among task points. The decoder, utilizing an attention network, decodes the encoded information provided by the encoder to generate the task selection sequence for each robot. We use a policy-based reinforcement learning approach to train the MamAM model. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the MamAM model through a series of comparative experiments. The findings reveal that, compared to non-learning-based methods for solving this problem, the MamAM model performs better in terms of inference speed and task completion rate.

articleTitle: Q-HIRL: A Q-Network Representation-Based Request Framework for Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning (HIRL) has emerged as a promising approach to address the challenges of sample efficiency and exploration in complex environments. This paper introduces a novel HIRL method called Q-HIRL (Q-Network Representation-Based Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning), which leverages Q-network representations to guide expert interventions and enhance learning efficiency. Unlike traditional methods that rely solely on Q-value differences, Q-HIRL utilizes the similarity between Q-network representations to determine when to request human guidance, resulting in more stable and efficient learning. The proposed approach dynamically adjusts the timing of expert interventions based on the convergence of representation similarity, adapting to different environments and improving overall robustness. Extensive experiments conducted across five MuJoCo environments demonstrate that Q-HIRL outperforms state-of-the-art HIRL methods and traditional reinforcement learning algorithms in terms of convergence speed and sample efficiency. Notably, Q-HIRL achieves superior results while requiring fewer human expert interventions compared to existing approaches.

articleTitle: Hound Tracking Optimization Algorithm Used to PSS, UPFC-POD Controller Parameter Optimization to Enhance Stability of WPTB System
abstract: In this paper, the hound tracking optimization algorithm (HTOA) is used to coordinate and optimize the parameters of the power system stabilizer (PSS), the unified power flow with power oscillation damping (UPFC-POD), to improve the damping characteristics of the WPTB system. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through experiments, and it can effectively slow down the oscillation amplitude of the system, maintain the system's stability, suppress the fluctuation of generator active and bus voltage caused by low-frequency oscillation (LFO), and improve the system's anti-interference capability.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Fixed-Time Control for Multiagent Systems with Actuator Faults
abstract: This paper investigates a reinforcement learning-based fixed-time tracking control scheme for multiagent systems against actuator faults. Firstly, an optimal control scheme is presented based on the simplified optimized control. In the optimization process, synchronization errors are embedded into the cost function, which promotes the achievement of the optimization task. Then, a novel actor-critic algorithm is designed to improve the convergence rate of system signals. Moreover, actuator faults are addressed to maintain the system performance. Finally, the presented optimized method ensures that all signals of the closed-loop system are bounded, and the simulation example verifies the feasibility of the presented control scheme.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Based Asymptotically Tracking Control for Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper studies an adaptive dynamic event-triggered consensus asymptotical tracking control problem for nonlinear multi-agent systems. A distributed parameter adaptive law is designed to compensate for the parameter uncertainty involved in the acquisition of adjacency information by the agent. An event-triggered strategy with dynamic threshold is designed to reduce transmission load and controller updates. By reasonably constructing the dynamics of triggering threshold, the derived dynamic event-triggered control protocol can guarantee zero-error tracking and eliminate Zeno behavior. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the developed scheme and the rationality of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Accelerated Projection Neurodynamic Approach for Convex Optimization with Affine Equality and Inequality Constraints
abstract: This paper presents an accelerated projection neurodynamic approach to deal with convex optimization issues that involve affine equality, inequality, and set constraints. The approach comprises two first-order projection ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for primal variables, two first-order ODEs for dual variables of the equation constraint, and two first-order projection ODEs for dual variables of the inequality constraint. A new projection strategy is introduced for the optimization variables and the dual variables of inequality constraints. This strategy not only can ensure the optimality of the neurodynamic method but also can be well integrated with the primal-dual dynamic method and the Nesterov accelerated dynamic method. By meeting specific parameter conditions, it is shown that the presented approach possesses a fast convergence rate comparable to that of the Nesterov accelerated gradient method. The effectiveness of the proposed projection neurodynamic approach is validated through numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Controllability and Synchronizability of Structural Brain Networks in Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Alzheimers disease (AD) is a degenerative disorder of the central nervous system, characterized by progressive cognitive dysfunction and behavioral impairment. However, the impact of AD on structural brain networks remains unclear. To investigate the differences in structural brain networks between the cognitive normal (CN) and AD groups, we use diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data from 30 subjects (15 CN subjects and 15 patients with AD) from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). We then apply network controllability theory and explore these differences by selecting three indicators: average controllability, modal controllability and synchronizability. Using these indicators, the support vector machine is employed to classify the two groups. Our results suggest that there are significant differences in the structural brain networks between the CN and AD groups in certain brain regions. Furthermore, the three indicators can effectively classify the two groups.

articleTitle: PFACO: Potential Field Ant Colony Optimization for Mobile Robot Path Planning
abstract: In response to the challenge of global path planning difficulties for automated guided vehicle in complex environments, traditional ant colony algorithms face several issues such as long search times, unordered search, and difficulty in finding the optimal route. We propose an optimized ant colony algorithm with potential field, named PFACO, that combines heuristic search and artificial potential field methods, along with the utilization of the pruning algorithm for secondary optimization of turning points. Specifically, we introduce improved potential fields and design heuristic functions to guide ants to swiftly navigate through unordered search states. After that, we incorporate the Triangle Pruning Algorithm (TPA) to perform secondary optimization by connecting turning points along the path. Simulation experiments demonstrate that PFACO, compared to both traditional Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithms and other improved ACO algorithms, achieves an average improvement of 93% and 78% in convergence speed, and an average optimization of 25.26% and 3.25% in path length, respectively, across various map conditions. The results show that PFACO has better global search capability, higher quality of convergence to the optimal solution, shorter generated path lengths, and greater robustness than other variants of the ant colony algorithm.

articleTitle: Electroencephalogram Emotion Classification Method Based on Spatial Hierarchical Attention Mechanism
abstract: Different odor sources result in various emotions and induce various Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals in the brain. Therefore, the classification of the EEG signals is important to understand brain activity. To solve this issue, an emotion classification method using olfactory EEG signals based on the convolutional neural network and spatial layered attention mechanism is proposed in this work. The convolutional neural network is employed to extract features of EEG signals from multiple vector spaces. The attention mechanism is used to fuse features, which can realize the judgment of human emotions. Experiments are conducted on Kato's dataset and compared with traditional machine algorithms using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores. The performance is improved by 16.80%, 18.30%, 18.72%, and 24.80% respectively, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: OSA-Net: A Deep Learning Approach for Obstructive Sleep Apnea Classification Using ECG Scalograms
abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a serious sleep-related respiratory disorder, marked by periodic interruptions in breathing, leading to severe cardiovascular complications. Due to the complexity and labor demands of polysomnography (PSG), early diagnosis of OSA remains challenging. To address this, this study proposes an automatic classification approach called the Obstructive Sleep Apnea Network (OSA-Net). This model uses ECG scalograms generated through wavelet transform for automatic OSA detection. OSA-Net effectively captures complex dynamic features while preserving dependencies between local information and global context. Extensive experiments on the Apnea-ECG dataset, using five-fold cross-validation, demonstrate the proposed framework's outstanding performance, achieving an accuracy of 0.910, sensitivity of 0.886, specificity of 0.933, and an F1 score of 0.907. These results highlight the potential of the proposed method in assisting clinical decision-making in OSA diagnosis.

articleTitle: Passivity Analysis of Reaction-Diffusion FCNNs with General Boundary Conditions and Impulsive Effects
abstract: This paper analyzes the passivity of reaction-diffusion fuzzy cellular neural networks (FCNNs) with general boundary conditions and impulse effects. By applying a Lyapunov function and utilizing various inequality techniques, we derive sufficient conditions for the passivity of these networks.

articleTitle: Dual Asynchronous Event-Triggered Control for Semi-Markov Jump Systems and Its Application
abstract: This paper studies the issue of dual asynchronous event-triggered control for semi-Markov jump systems. Considering the disturbance and time delay, it is difficult to guarantee the synchronous operation of the modes among the system, event generator and controller. Moreover, limited network resources need to be saved in practice. To this end, asynchronous eventtriggered scheme and controller are established simultaneously. Meanwhile, sufficient conditions are established to ensure that event-triggered parameters and controller gains can be obtained. Finally, the validity of the proposed method is verified through its application to a single-link robot arm model.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning Deraining Network Based on Multi-Scale CycleGAN Architecture
abstract: In outdoor vision systems like autonomous driving, traffic monitoring, and drone imaging, rain can significantly degrade image quality and affect task accuracy. To address this, we propose a multi-scale CycleGAN-based contrastive learning deraining network. Using unpaired rainy and clear images, the network enhances deraining through generative adversarial networks and contrastive learning. Generator G converts rainy images into clear ones, while generator F simulates the degradation from clear to rainy images. Discriminators Dclear and Drain evaluate the authenticity of the generated images. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively removes rain streaks and improves image quality in complex scenes, offering a solution for single-image deraining

articleTitle: Memristive Bionic Circuit Design of Episodic Memory Generation and Recall Related to Olfaction
abstract: The design of olfactory bionic circuits is an important part in brain-like intelligence. It has a wide application prospect in the fields of environmental monitoring, disaster warning and unmanned rescue. Episodic memory is an important memory pattern of human brain, which has a deep connection with olfaction. It is promising to study olfactory perception and episodic memory for brain-like perception and information processing in robots. Based on the olfactory perception mechanism and memristor, this work designs a bionic circuit of olfactory episodic memory generation and recall, which simulates the process of olfactory episodic memory generation and recall with the phenomenon of olfactory adaptation, which accords with the physiological connection between olfaction and episodic memory. The simulation results show that the circuit can simulate the process of generating and recalling episodic memory through olfaction, which lays a foundation for the robot to establish the correlation between sensory perception and memory.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Order-Enabled Contrastive Learning-Based Dual Autoencoder Fault Detection for Variable Speed Bearing
abstract: Bearing fault detection is crucial in ensuring the reliability and safety of rotating machinery, as undetected faults can lead to unexpected equipment failure and costly down-time. Traditional fault detection methods particularly based on constant speed assumptions, face challenges in handling the complexities of variable speed conditions. In this paper, we propose a fault detection method for bearings under variable-speed conditions, combining order information and contrastive learning. Specifically, the impact of speed variations is effectively mitigated through angular resampling. Then, order envelope signals are extracted to amplify weak signals. Subsequently, a contrastive learning-based dual-channel asymmetric autoencoder structure is introduced, where two autoencoders independently process and reconstruct signals. By minimizing the contrastive loss between hidden layers of normal samples, the model learns the inherent consistency of normal data representations. This consistency allows the model to detect abnormalities by identifying deviations in contrastive loss. Experiments validate the performance of the proposed method in detecting bearing faults under variable speed conditions.

articleTitle: Distributed Optimization via Mixing ADAM and Quasi-Newton Methods
abstract: The heterogeneous computational capacities of devices always negatively impact the performance of distributed optimization algorithms. In this paper, we propose a novel distributed optimization algorithm based on a mixture of different local optimizers, termed as FedMix, which has the potential to leverage the heterogeneity to enhance the performance. Specifically, FedMix is designed in the parameter-server framework, and each client can be equipped with either an Adam optimizer or a quasi-Newton optimizer for local updates based on its computational capability, which leads to a mixture of Adam and Quasi-Newton in our algorithm. As different local optimizers demand different computational capabilities, our algorithm FedMix can achieve better alignment between algorithms and computing resources, facilitating improved performance especially in the heterogeneous computational environment. Sufficient experiments are presented to substantiate the superior performance of our algorithm by comparing with existing algorithms.

articleTitle: A Predefined-Time Adaptive Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a predefined-time adaptive algorithm for the optimization problem with private inequality constraints. By designing algorithms, penalty parameters are designed to handle private inequality constraints, and through adaptive penalties, the parameters in the algorithm are adaptively adjusted according to the degree of violation of private inequality constraints by the state solution. Moreover, The smoothing method is also integrated into adaptive penalty, overcoming the difficulty of non smooth dynamic behavior of the objective function and adaptive penalty parameters. In addition, a predefined-time mechanism is introduced to enable the algorithm to converge within the predefined-time.

articleTitle: Non-Autonomous ReLU-Type Hopfield Neural Network Model
abstract: Neural networks play a crucial role in neuromorphic computing and intelligent systems. For the Hopfield neural networks (HNN), despite much research focus on autonomous models, practical scenarios often involve external influences with time-varying stimuli, which requires exploration of the dynamical effects on the non-autonomous HNN model. This study investigates a simple ReLU-type HNN model with alternating current (AC) inputs first. Then, the ones influenced by the amplitude parameter are revealed. Numerical results confirm that complex phenomena occur including chaos, quasi-period, transient states, and coexisting attractors. Finally, an electrical circuit is used to verify the influence of a time-varying external environment on such a neural network, and the measured results on the analog level are consistent with the numerical simulations. Certainly, such the neural network will disclose the behaviors of large-scale network clusters and the engineering applications of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Fire Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
abstract: Fire identification plays a crucial role in the realm of fire safety, serving as a vital component for the early detection and swift response to fire incidents. Effective fire identification is essential in minimizing the damage and losses associated with fires, as it enables timely interventions. we introduce a novel fire detection method that employs RHE-YOLOv8, aiming to enhance the accuracy of fire identification and localization. By leveraging this advanced approach, we seek to optimize the response speed of fire identification systems, ultimately facilitating more precise recognition and pinpointing of fire sources. In this study, the YOLOv8 model incorporates the RepGhost module to decrease its floating-point computations, thus achieving a more lightweight structure. Furthermore, the seamless integration of the Hyb-ECA attention mechanism into the network's neck structure has notably boosted the model's recognition accuracy, all while maintaining a low computational footprint. Experimental findings demonstrate that these enhancements can elevate the average precision (mAP) of the YOLOv8 model by 2.5%. Simultaneously, the model undergoes a decrease in floating-point operations (GFLOPs) of 13.6%. These enhancements significantly improve both the precision and effectiveness of fire detection, demonstrating their efficacy in real-world fire situations.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Control for Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems via Dynamic Event-Triggered Mechanism
abstract: In the case where the multi-agent network contains a directed spanning tree and the topology between followers forms an undirected connected graph, this paper studies the consensus problem of nonlinear leader-following multi-agent systems with external disturbances. An adaptive neural network control strategy based on the states of neighboring agents is proposed. To address the resource constraints caused by the neural network and communication, dynamic event-triggered mechanism is introduced. Through rigorous theoretical analysis and proofs, it is demonstrated that the proposed control strategy can ensure that the multi-agent system converges to a stable equilibrium state under external disturbances and achieves state consensus.

articleTitle: FRMAdam-iTransformer KAN: A Fractional Order RMS Momentum Adam Optimized iTransformer with KAN for EEG and ECG Prediction
abstract: Accurately predicting electrocardiogram (ECG) and electroencephalogram (EEG) signals holds significant clinical importance. Although the iTransformer model performs well in long-sequence predictions, it still faces challenges such as low computational efficiency and gradient explosion. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fractional order root mean square momentum adaptive moment estimation optimizer iTransformer model based on Kolmogorov Arnold (FRMAdam-iTransformer KAN). This model incorporates the Fractional Root Mean Square Momentum Adaptive Moment Estimation optimizer (FRMAdam) and replaces the fully connected output layer of the original iTransformer with a KAN structure to improve prediction accuracy. Experimental results on ECG and EEG datasets demonstrate that the FRMAdam-iTransformer KAN model achieves a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0004 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0137, representing reductions of 76.47% and 59.59%, respectively, compared to the original iTransformer model.

articleTitle: Preassigned-Time Stabilization of Memristive Chaotic Circuit via Switching Control
abstract: In this paper, we propose a 3D memristive chaotic circuit, in which both its dynamical behaviors and the preassigned-time stability are analyzed. First, we design a chaotic circuit utilizing the KNOWM memristor model, and confirm the presence of chaos through phase portrait. Subsequently, we develop a switching controller, which successfully achieves the preassigned-time stability of the memristive chaotic circuit. Ultimately, the validity of our theoretical findings is substantiated through rigorous numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Images Encryption and Transmission for Neuromorphic Systems Based on Chaotic Dynamic Behaviors
abstract: In neuromorphic computing, robust image encryption is crucial for safeguarding sensitive data. This paper introduces an innovative one-dimensional logistic-sine chaotic map that generates highly unpredictable and resistant-to-statistical-analysis sequences, making them difficult to decipher. In the proposed image encryption algorithm, we employ a dynamic key generation algorithm to generate encryption keys, thereby reducing the risk of key leakage or reuse. Furthermore, by utilizing block inter-plane scrambling and dynamic pixel diffusion, our image encryption algorithm achieves a high level of encryption quality. Notably, the Discrete Wavelet Transform is used to embed the cipher image into a carrier image, reducing the risk of interception during transmission. Extensive experimentation and evaluation on specific scene images demonstrate the excellent performance of the proposed image encryption algorithm in terms of security and confidentiality: the devised encryption scheme attains an NPCR of 99.6197% and UACI of 33.2966%, along with an average entropy of 7.9994, making it highly suitable for neuromorphic applications.

articleTitle: Saturated Impulsive Distributed Filtering for Target Estimation Over Sensor Networks
abstract: This study introduces an impulsive filtering strategy with saturation to mitigate hardware damage caused by excessive gains in sensor networks, addressing energy optimization challenges in target estimation. The saturation introduces non-linearity, tackled through sector conditions and Lyapunov stability, to derive conditions for asymptotic estimation with saturated impulses. The approach's efficacy is validated via simulations in a network of four sensor groups.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technologies of Object Detection in Autonomous Driving Environments Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Autonomous driving demands object detection with high accuracy and real-time performance to assist environmental perception by identifying pedestrians, vehicles, traffic signs, and more. However, challenges remain in balancing speed and accuracy, as well as handling complex lighting conditions and object occlusion. This study explores commonly used object detection methods in autonomous driving, including two-stage detectors and single-stage detectors. It further analyzes how feature extraction, multi-scale detection, lightweight networks, and data augmentation techniques enhance model performance. Through optimization strategies such as model compression, pruning, and quantization, the study achieves a balance between model accuracy and detection speed. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized model achieves high real-time performance and accuracy on datasets like COCO and KITTI, with superior results in terms of mean Average Precision (mAP) and Frames Per Second (FPS) compared to unoptimized models, showcasing its potential for autonomous driving applications.

articleTitle: Edge Detection Circuit Based on Memristive Crossbar Array with Adaptive Thresholding and Morphological Processing
abstract: This paper presents a novel edge detection method using a memristor-based array, which integrates image feature extraction, adaptive binarization, and morphological processing into a unified hardware system. The proposed approach leverages the memristor array to simultaneously perform horizontal and vertical feature extraction and apply an adaptive thresholding technique based on row and column averages. This in-situ processing minimizes data transfer and computation overhead, significantly reducing power consumption while enhancing edge detection robustness. Furthermore, morphological operations such as erosion and dilation are incorporated to refine edge continuity and noise suppression.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8-Based Pest Identification Method for Farmland
abstract: In response to the problems of large model parameters and high computational requirements in existing farmland pest identification models, an enhanced pest identification approach based on YOLOv8 for farmland has been put forward. This approach aims to lower the computational burden and memory consumption while enhancing the target detection speed. The approach incorporates a lightweight convolutional module, GhostConv, in the Backbone layer to substitute the common convolution in the original YOLOv8 feature extraction network, thereby reducing the network parameters. Furthermore, a lightweight C3Ghost module is introduced to replace the original C2f module in the feature extraction network, further reducing the computational load. Tests on a constructed farmland pest dataset indicate that compared with the YOLOv8 model, the mAP value of the improved model reaches 90.8%, which is basically equivalent to that of the YOLOv8 model; the computational load is reduced from 8.1 GFLoPs to 5.0 GFLoPs, a decrease of 38.3%. Compared to the current mainstream object detection algorithms, the improved model demands fewer computational resources and is faster without sacrificing detection accuracy, giving it an edge in deployment, especially in scenarios with limited resources or requiring real-time processing. This optimization is highly valuable for applications that aim to reduce computational costs and improve response speed while maintaining high precision.

articleTitle: Robust Lattice Kalman Filter Under False Data Injection Attacks and Measurement Data Loss
abstract: In this paper, a novel model under false data injection (FDI) attack and measurement loss is established, and it is combined with lattice Kalman filter (LKF). LKF based on loss and generalized measurement model (LGMM) is proposed as an effective method for dealing with simultaneous measurement loss and FDI attacks. LGMM can be extended to other nonlinear Kalman filters, such as extended Kalman filter (EKF), unscented Kalman filter (UKF), and cubature Kalman filter (CKF). Furthermore, in order to make the estimation more accurate, a back out step is added to the framework. The robustness and effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Study and Analysis of DTN Routing Algorithms Based on Mobility Speed Statistics in Unconventional Networks
abstract: In Delay Tolerant Networks (DTNs), which are a type of unconventional network, nodes are unable to obtain the global network topology, and both the speed and direction of node movement are random and uncertain. To facilitate information transmission, a “store-carry-forward” strategy is employed in DTNs. In practical scenarios with changing topology, nodes that move slowly can become “zombie” nodes, negatively impacting message delivery, increasing network latency, and reducing resource utilization. In light of this, selecting nodes with higher mobility for message replication can effectively improve Packet delivery rates and reduce delays. This paper proposes the MSSD routing algorithm for unconventional networks, based on mobility speed statistics. By utilizing the faster mobility of nodes, which broadens their reach and reduces delay, the algorithm better adapts to the unique environment of unconventional networks. Consequently, transmission delays are reduced. Simulations demonstrate that the MSSD algorithm is both effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Discriminative Features Learning for Fine-Grained Nuclear Cataract Classification in AS-OCT Images with Supervised Contrastive Learning
abstract: Currently, most methods for classifying nuclear cataracts (NC) rely on coarse-grained feature extraction techniques. This paper proposes a fine-grained classification model specifically designed to identify pathological regions with subtle differences. The model first utilizes a backbone to extract global features, followed by further processing of these global features to extract discriminative features. These regional features are then fused with the global features, and the combined features are fed into a classification head to generate classification probabilities. Additionally, a supervised contrastive learning strategy is applied to the global features. This strategy significantly improves the similarity between samples of the same class while increasing the differences between samples of different classes, thereby enhancing the representation of the global features and ultimately improving the classification performance of NC. The proposed network was tested on a local AS-OCT dataset for classification, where it demonstrated excellent performance, achieving a high classification accuracy 88.38%.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Optimal Control with Time Delays for Discrete-Time Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper investigates adaptive fault-tolerant optimal control for discrete-time multi-agent systems with time-varying input delays and actuator faults using reinforcement learning. A controller is developed via a policy iteration method to solve the discrete-time Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. In addition, actor-critic neural networks enable real-time approximation of the control input and performance index. An M network addresses input delays, while a fault compensation scheme mitigates actuator faults. Convergence and stability are proven, and numerical simulations validate effectiveness.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Control for Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems with Input Dead Zones
abstract: An adaptive real finite-time tracking control scheme is proposed for a specific class of nonlinear systems characterized by input dead zones. This scheme is based on Lyapunov finitetime stability theory and the backstepping control algorithm, utilizing neural networks to approximate unknown nonlinear functions effectively. The designed protocols ensure that the system can achieve satisfactory tracking performance, with all signals in the closed-loop system being semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. To validate the proposed control strategy, a simulation example is conducted, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: HLSM-UNet:Hybrid Local Spatial Mamba UNet for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: In the field of Medical Image Segmentation, deep learning models, especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) models, have been widely researched and applied in recent years. However, these two mainstream methods each face some challenges. CNN occupies a place in medical image processing with its powerful local feature extraction ability, but it is inadequate in dealing with global or remote feature dependencies, which to some extent limits its performance in complex medical image segmentation tasks. The ViT model, through its Self-Attention mechanism, can effectively capture long-range dependencies in images, but it also comes with high computational costs, especially the secondary computational complexity, which becomes a bottleneck that cannot be ignored when processing high-resolution medical images. In this paper, we propose a medical image segmentation method called HLSM-UNet based on a State Space Model(SSM). This model combines the advantages of UNet with the remote modeling capability of the Mamba model, aiming to achieve more efficient and accurate medical image segmentation. We conducted experiments on the publicly available ACDC MRI heart segmentation dataset and Prostate dataset, and the results showed that HLSM UNet outperforms existing CNN and Transformer models in multiple evaluation metrics. Especially in terms of remote modeling capability and computational efficiency, significant advantages have been demonstrated. This not only proves the effectiveness of the state space model in medical image segmentation, but also provides new ideas and methods for subsequent research.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Consensus of Leader-Following Multi-Agent Systems Under Sliding Mode Control with External Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the predefined-time(PT) consensus problem of leader-following multi-agent systems(MASs) under sliding mode(SME) control with external disturbance(ED), and Considers the dynamic system models of the first-order (FOR) and second-order(SOR) nonlinear nodes. Firstly, an integral sliding mode controller is designed for first-order nonlinear nodes to ensure the stability and consensus of first-order multi-agents within a pre-defined time. Secondly, a non-singular terminal is provided for second -order nonlinear nodes to address the singularity of the controller and to achieve the consensus of nonlinear nodes within a pre-defined time. Thirstly, the system's consensus is demonstrated by the Lyapunov function. The time parameters for reaching the sliding mode can be set in advance and adjusted. Finally, two examples are proposed to verify the validity and rationality of the model.

articleTitle: Cluster Synchronization for Coupled Neural Networks with Mixed Couplings via Pinning Partial Impulsive Strategy
abstract: This paper explores the issue of cluster synchronization (CS) for coupled neural networks (CNNs) with both current-state coupling and distributed-delay coupling using a pinning partial impulsive control (PPIC) strategy. Considering the synchronization of an array of neural networks featuring two distinct topologies and targeting a desired trajectory while reducing control costs, a novel PPIC strategy is proposed, which selectively controls a specific subset of neurons within certain subnetworks. Finally, the validity of the theoretical analysis and the proposed control scheme is demonstrated through a numerical example.

articleTitle: Bearing-Based Formation Control Using Reset Protocol
abstract: This paper develops a reset control strategy for bearing-based formation of first-order multi-agent systems, combining the agents' bearing measurements with relative position information. This is particularly advantageous in scenarios with limited sensory data. The approach introduced in this work integrates a reset mechanism into the bearing-based formation dynamics, enhancing the precision of inter-agent bearings and speeding up the formation process, thus providing a more accurate control mechanism in comparison to the traditional bearing-based formation protocol. The effectiveness of this method is validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Secure Synchronization of Neural Networks by Pinning Partial Impulsive Control
abstract: This paper investigates the secure synchronization of complex dynamic networks (CDNs) under Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. A novel control-theoretic framework based on pinning impulsive control is proposed, and sufficient conditions for achieving secure synchronization are derived using Lyapunov-based methods. Finally, the effectiveness of the approach is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: NODE-Former: A Hybrid Approach for Robust Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
abstract: The accurate prediction of electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals proves crucial for clinical diagnosis. However, the long-term time series prediction still faces challenges such as the strong dependence on training samples and poor extrapolation performance. To address these issues, This paper introduces NODE-Former (Neural Ordinary Differential Equations-Former), a model designed for accurate long-term prediction of EEG and ECG signals, the model uses latent states with probsparse attention to encode time series and neural ordinary differential equations (NODE) to infer correlations, improving the extrapolation performance. A fractional optimizer is introduced to retain more historical information, enhancing memory, stability, and convergence speed. NODE-Former effectively reconstructs time series and demonstrates superior inference on unseen data. In tests on the MIT-BIH Polysomnographic Database, it outperforms the ITransformer by 77% and NODE-RNN by 48%.

articleTitle: A Bionic Circuit for Emotion Associative Memory Based on Memristive Neural Networks
abstract: Bionics-driven brain-inspired intelligence is a vital component of the field of artificial intelligence. Constructing bionic circuits for emotional associative memory enables the simulation of human brain functions such as learning, forgetting, and memory. Two similar emotions, namely fear and disgust, are introduced in this study. Since the synaptic structures between different emotions vary, distinct emotional modules are designed to simulate these two similar emotions. The circuit consists of four modules: the fear emotion logic module, which selects corresponding functions by determining the activation states of fear-related language and auditory signals; the fear emotion synapse module, responsible for implementing the learning or forgetting functions of fear; the disgust emotion logic module, which selects corresponding functions by determining the activation states of disgust-related language and auditory signals; and the disgust emotion synapse module, responsible for implementing the learning or forgetting functions of disgust. The effects of these two similar emotions on associative memory were evaluated using PSpice simulations, demonstrating distinct impacts on emotional associative memory.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Many-to-Many Associative Memory Driven by External Input
abstract: The many-to-many associative memory is a brain-inspired functionality, which includes one-to-many and many-to-one associations. Most models neglected the inherent relationships of the input patterns or output patterns. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cascaded multivalued continuous-time recurrent neural networks, where the current network's output is linked with both its own input and the output of the previous network. The global asymptotic convergence of equilibrium points is leveraged to design a learning algorithm based on inequalities. Compared to multidirectional associative memory networks, this model can reflect the temporal and inherent relationships of the inputs or outputs, requires fewer neurons for the associative process, and imposes no constraints on the initial state of the neurons.

articleTitle: Bumpless Transfer Synchronization of Delayed Chaotic Neural Networks by Intermittent Control
abstract: This work handles the bumpless transfer (BT) exponential synchronization of delayed chaotic systems via periodically intermittent control. A BT intermittent controller is designed via the gain interpolation. Under the Lyapunov functional theory, a sufficient condition ensuring the synchronization between the master system and the slave system is derived. A procedure to get the BT intermittent controller is also proposed. The effectiveness of the presented results is shown by the Lu neural oscillator.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of High-Order Rotor Hopfield Neural Networks and Dense Associative Memory: Structural Similarities and Functional Differences
