abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of Highorder Rotor Hopfield Neural Networks (HRHNNs) and Dense Associative Memory (DAM) models, highlighting their structural similarities and functional differences in associative memory tasks. Both models use energy functions to store patterns as lowenergy states, but they vary in handling multi-valued patterns and synaptic architectures. HRHNNs leverage high-order connections and multi-body synapses, which enhance their capacity for multivalued pattern storage and retrieval. In contrast, DAM operates with binary patterns and employs an energy difference learning algorithm. The experiments target multi-valued associative memory tasks for both HRHNNs and DAM. Results show that HRHNNs outperform DAM under high load factors and complex multi-valued tasks, while DAM demonstrates robustness with a larger number of patterns. This work emphasizes the potential of integrating biologically interpretable synaptic structures into artificial neural networks to enhance associative memory performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of a Stochastic Rumor Model with Media Coverage and Whistleblowing Mechanism
abstract: Considering the influence of whistleblowing mechanism and media coverage, a novel stochastic rumor propagation model along with stochastic disturbance is proposed in this article. Firstly, the existence of a global positive solution is proved by defining the stop time. Secondly, sufficient conditions of the extinction and persistence are derived by means of the strong law of large numbers and Itô's formula. Finally, numerical simulations indicate that the effectiveness and rationality of the model.

articleTitle: Attack Time Consensus Control for 3D Multi-Missile Systems Based on Adaptive Dynamic Programming
abstract: This investigation focuses on a collaborative control framework developed using a three-dimensional(3D) nonlinear guidance architecture. For the multi-missile system in 3D coordinate system, time-to-go and adaptive dynamic programming methods are used to control the motion of each missile simultaneously. In the Line-of-sight (LOS) coordinate system, the acceleration component along the LOS direction can make the attack time consensus of multi-missile system. The acceleration components in the direction of pitch Angle and deflection Angle are used for precise navigation. By leveraging adaptive dynamic programming (ADP), the proposed framework ensures synchronized attack timing across the multi-missile network while minimizing energy expenditure. The efficacy of the proposed approach is ultimately validated through computational modeling and simulation analysis.

articleTitle: DEGAN: A Deep Learning Model for SAR Image Segmentation in Aquacultural Raft Monitoring
abstract: Offshore aquacultural raft information extraction from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is crucial for large-scale marine resource exploitation and environmental protection. In this paper, a deep learning model named Detail-Enhancing Generative Adversarial Network (DEGAN) is proposed for SAR image segmentation to monitor aquacultural rafts. DEGAN incorporates several key modules to enhance segmentation performance, including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>-divergence to improve the discrim-inator's ability to handle noisy data, and the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for more effective spatial and channel attention. Within CBAM, multi-scale feature fusion is employed to capture both fine and coarse details across different resolutions. Additionally, the Simple, Parameter-Free Attention Module (SimAM) is introduced to enhance feature refinement by deriving neuron importance through an energy function. These modules, when integrated into the GAN framework, work together to improve noise suppression and detail preservation, critical for accurate segmentation in challenging SAR images. Experimental results demonstrate that DEGAN outperforms five baseline models in four performance metrics, making it highly effective for aquacultural raft monitoring in complex marine environments.

articleTitle: Geomagnetic/Inertial Fusion Indoor Navigation System Based on an Improved WD-UKF*
abstract: Accurate indoor positioning has become increasingly important as the demand for high-precision navigation grows. However, traditional single-sensor technologies struggle to meet these requirements. This paper presents an enhanced geomagnetic/inertial fusion navigation system based on a Wavelet Denoising-Unscented Kalman Filter (WD-UKF). The system integrates geomagnetic and inertial data, decomposing the signals into multi-frequency components using wavelet transform, followed by denoising through an optimized thresholding function. Nonlinear state estimation of the denoised components is performed using the Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF). Evaluations in complex indoor environments show that the proposed WD-UKF significantly mitigates noise and improves positioning accuracy, achieving a maximum spindle turning error of only 3.7 cm, These results demonstrate the system's robustness and precision, making it well-suited for dynamic and challenging indoor navigation scenarios.

articleTitle: Backstepping-Based Adaptive Formation Control of Quadrotor UAVs with Multiple Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) formation control subject to unknown external disturbances. The dynamics of UAVs are described by three-dimensional second-order nonlinear models, and the unknown nonlinear functions are approximated using the radial basis function neural networks. The disturbance filters are designed to convert the disturbance rejection problem into an adaptive tracking problem, then the values of the unknown disturbances are estimated based on the adaptive backstepping method, and the effect of the disturbances is eliminated. Lyapunov stability analysis supports the global uniform boundedness of all closed-loop signals. Finally, the simulation results prove the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Intelligent Monitoring and Analysis of Sports Data in the Context of Rural Revitalization Based on Federated Learning
abstract: With the advancement of the rural revitalization strategy, leveraging intelligent technologies to improve the efficiency of monitoring and analyzing rural sports data has become a hot topic of research. This study proposes an intelligent monitoring and analysis framework for sports data based on federated learning, tailored for the rural revitalization context to address challenges related to data privacy protection and data silos. First, a distributed architecture for sports data analysis is designed, enabling joint analysis without aggregating data from various regions, thereby ensuring data privacy. Second, the study provides an in -depth analysis of federated learning's privacy protection capabilities, model convergence, and computational efficiency, demonstrating the advantages of this approach. Finally, experiments conducted on real-world rural sports datasets validate the proposed framework through comparative analyses, highlighting its accuracy and efficiency. Results show that the federated learning-based method offers significant advantages in data protection, real-time monitoring, and model performance.

articleTitle: EMDepth: Self-Supervised Event-Based Monocular Depth Estimation
abstract: Event camera, a novel bionic vision sensor, fundamentally diverge from traditional imaging devices in their operational principles. Featuring high temporal resolution and extensive dynamic range, these sensors demonstrate exceptional performance in challenging imaging scenarios. However, the event streams generated by such cameras are inherently asynchronous, sparse, low spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratios, rendering direct application in conventional depth estimation methodologies problematic. In this study, we introduce EMDepth, a innovative monocular event camera-based scene depth estimation method. EMDepth innovatively preserves the spatial and temporal neighborhood characteristics of event points, enabling accurate scene depth reconstruction under low-light conditions and rapid motion scenarios. Experimental validation on the DSEC dataset substantiates the method's effectiveness, demonstrating superior performance compared to current supervised event-driven and unsupervised image-based approaches.

articleTitle: KAN Convolution for Image Classification
abstract: This paper introduces a convolutional method called KAN convolution, designed to replace traditional convolutional layers in the ResNet architecture. The KAN convolution is inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), which leverage B-spline functions to model univariate functions, allowing for more effective feature extraction and better representation of complex data patterns. Our approach aims to address the limitations of conventional convolutional layers in capturing hierarchical and contextual relationships within the data. By integrating KAN convolution into ResNet, the modified model demonstrates improved performance in image classification tasks across various benchmark datasets. The proposed method is thoroughly evaluated on three widely used datasets: CIFAR10, CIFAR-100-20, and STL-10. The evaluation metrics include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, providing a comprehensive assessment of classification performance. Experimental results show that ResNet models with KAN convolution consistently outperform their traditional counterparts on complex datasets, particularly CIFAR-100-20 and STL-10. Moreover, the introduction of KAN convolution leads to more stable training and enhanced generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: A Multi-Scale CNN-LSTM Network with Squeeze and Excitation Block for Leg Movement Detection during Sleep
abstract: Detection of leg movements during sleep is crucial for diagnosing periodic limb movement syndrome and restless leg syndrome. However, there are significant differences in the manual scoring of leg movement in nocturnal polysomnography studies. Therefore, we propose a CNN-LSTM network specifically designed for classifying sleep leg movement events. By leveraging the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, our approach effectively captures both local and global features for enhanced feature representation. Additionally, a multi-scale convolutional (MC) module and the squeeze and excitation (SE) module are introduced with the purpose of extracting features at different scales and frequencies and weakening redundant features for better performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our network outperforms previous baseline methods in detecting sleep leg movement events on the pubulic dataset.

articleTitle: Using Memoryless Dual Observers for Tracking Consensus in Multi-Agent Systems with Input and Output Delays
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of dual-observer-based trajectory tracking of the leader for multi-agent systems(MASs) with delays in both inputs and outputs. Through the model reduction method, the system can be transformed into an equivalent linear system without delays, allowing for the design of a dual-observer-based stabilizing controller. This controller is memory-based. To address this issue, an improved memoryless dual-observer-based stabilizing controller is designed, and it is proven that the trajectory of the leader can be tracked under certain additional conditions. This design method is more challenging in achieving the trajectory tracking of the leader, for example, requiring the construction of a more complex Lyapunov-Krasovskii function. Numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Trigonometric Expansion based Random Fourier Feature Algorithm for Nonlinear Adaptive Filtering
abstract: Traditional nonlinear adaptive filters that rely solely on either functional link network (FLN) or kernel method encounter constraints in their capabilities of nonlinear modeling. This paper presents a novel nonlinear adaptive filter that inte-grates both FLN and kernel method to improve estimation performance in dealing with nonlinear filtering problems. By employing trigonometric expansion to create FLN model and random Fourier feature (RFF) technique to design kernel method, a novel trigonometric expansion based random Fourier feature (TERFF) algorithm relying on stochastic gradient descent optimization is derived. Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed algorithm in terms of filtering accuracy.

articleTitle: NN-Based Prescribed-Time Control for Nonlinear Multiagent Systems with Switching Topologies
abstract: This paper focuses on prescribed-time control for nonlinear multiagent systems (MASs) with switching topologies. To address the discontinuity issue of the reference signal caused by switching communication topologies, a distributed estimator is devised to obtain a bounded continuous reference signal. Subsequently, a high-order filter is introduced to generate a high-order differential reference signal. Furthermore, a prescribed-time consensus control protocol is developed, which ensures the tracking error remains within a prescribed range during the prescribed time from any initial position. The unknown nonlinearities within the MASs are approximated using neural networks. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control protocol is validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Mean-Square Exponential Stability of Stochastic Complex-Valued Neural Networks with Impulses
abstract: This paper studies the mean-square exponential stability of stochastic complex-valued neural networks (SCVNNs) with impulses. Using a Lyapunov function and the complex Itô formula, sufficient conditions for stability are derived. Numerical examples are provided to verify the results.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Observer-Based Fixed-Time Consensus Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Multiagent Systems with Unknown States
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for achieving fixed-time tracking consensus control in multiagent systems (MASs). Departing from the reliance on traditional controllers, our innovative controller integrates modified tuning and Lyapunov functions to guarantee stability and convergence. Furthermore, we have implemented an event-triggered strategy aimed at reducing the frequency of updates, alongside an output-feedback observer to manage unmeasured states effectively. To address the challenges posed by unknown functions and algebraic-loop problems, we opted for radial basis function neural networks (RBF NNs), chosen for their superior performance. Our methodology successfully mitigates Zeno's behavior and ensures stability within a narrowly defined set. The efficacy of our proposed solution is validated through two illustrative simulation examples.

articleTitle: KM-Prompt: A Prompt-Based CNN for Continual Learning
abstract: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in many applications but often suffer from catastrophic forgetting—a significant drop in performance on previously learned tasks when training on new ones. Continual learning seeks to address this challenge. A straightforward yet effective solution is to replay a subset of past data, though this strategy increases memory costs and can raise concerns over data privacy. Recently, prompt-based methods have gained considerable attention, as they can achieve strong performance without requiring a rehearsal buffer. In this work, we are the first to introduce a prompt-based method to the CNN framework, breaking the previous reliance on Transformers. By leveraging kernel prompts and mask prompts to tune the CNN backbone, our model captures task-specific patterns while filtering out irrelevant information from feature maps. Prompts are combined based on the similarity between features and queries, enabling dynamic selection of knowledge. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our method, with improvements of over 0.8% and 7% in average final accuracy on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-R, respectively, compared to classic methods.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Passivity and Synchronization of Spatiotemporal Networks with Multiple Weights via Boundary Control
abstract: This article focuses on fixed-time passivity and synchronization for multi-weighted spatiotemporal networks with mixed boundary condition. Firstly, a kind of boundary control scheme is developed, which is implemented on the right boundary. Subsequently, several fixed-time passivity criteria are established by making use of inequality technique and Lyapunov method. In addition, in the light of obtained fixed-time output-strict passivity result, a fixed-time synchronization criterion for the spatiotemporal networks with multiple weights is naturally gained, and the upper bound of the synchronization time is estimated based on fixed-time stability theory. Finally, a simulation example is proposed to verify the availability of the derived results.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Recurrent Neural Network for Traffic Flow Forecasting
abstract: As a core function of intelligent transportation systems (ITSs), traffic flow forecasting (TFF) is crucial for reducing congestion in urban areas. Although existing studies have made progress in modeling spatiotemporal dependencies within traffic networks, they ignore the deeper correlations between spatiotemporal features and are particularly deficient in capturing long-distance spatial dependencies and complex dynamic temporal features. To address the aforesaid issues, this paper proposes a Bidirectional Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Recurrent Neural Network (Bi-DSTGRNN) for TFF. Specifically, we construct a multi-head self-attention-based gated recurrent unit (MSA-GRU) mechanism to model complex dynamic features of the temporal sequence, utilizing multi-head self-attention to uncover global temporal dependencies, and a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU) is employed to extract long-term trends. we design a GraphSAGE-based dynamic graph neural network (DGraphSAGE), which dynamically aggregates node features and accurately represents both local and global information in road networks. Finally, we develop a multi-layer Chebyshev graph convolutional network to smooth node embeddings and efficiently extract the global dynamic topology of the traffic network. Experimental results on the PEMSD4 and PEMSD8 datasets demonstrate that the Bi-DSTGRNN model outperforms existing baseline models in prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Approach to Arm-Hand Robot Learning from Demonstration
abstract: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) is an effective method for equipping robots with manipulation skills, but it faces challenges due to fundamental differences between human and robotic systems. Most existing studies on LfD for arm-hand robots focus on learning arm trajectories, often neglecting the complete manipulation process. To address this limitation, we propose a novel learning framework for arm-hand robots. A depth camera captures datasets of movement trajectories and pose information from human demonstrations. These datasets are processed using Dynamical Movement Primitives (DMP) techniques, enhanced with obstacle avoidance and trajectory smoothing to improve the robot's ability to imitate and generalize trajectory information. An improved motion retargeting algorithm translates hand pose features into joint angle parameters, enabling the generation of diverse object grasping primitives for the robotic hand. A target detection algorithm triggers these primitives, integrating them with arm trajectories to create a comprehensive object manipulation strategy. The proposed framework was validated on the UR5 robotic arm and Inspire dexterous hand, successfully performing object grasping tasks on a desktop and demonstrating its effectiveness in complex manipulation scenarios.

articleTitle: A Novel Distributed Prescribed-Time Convergence Acceleration Algorithm with Time Rescaling
abstract: In this article, we present a novel distributed algorithm for prescribed-time convergence acceleration with time rescaling. Two novel prescribed-time acceleration algorithms are designed to tackle distributed unconstrained optimization problems and distributed optimization problems with constraints, effectively mirroring centralized optimization tasks within the framework of a closed convex set. We introduce several pivotal theorems, and the convergence of these algorithms are rigorously demonstrated through the application of Lyapunov functions. Finally, some comprehensive numerical simulations are conducted to validate the practicality and robustness of our theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Practical Consensus of DC Microgrid Secondary Control with Prescribed Performance
abstract: This article describes a secondary control method for islanded DC microgrids that is based on events and uses prescribed performance control to ensure required transient performance while sharing current and regulating voltage. The developed controller is capable of confining the deviations of both the bus voltage and current sharing within predefined bounds. A carefully designed event-triggering mechanism initiates control execution based on relative control error, while the developed controller ensures convergence with the specified transient performance of the microgrid system. The protocol guarantees that no converter displays Zeno behavior. Ultimately, we offer a simulation example to substantiate the practical performance of the proposed strategies.

articleTitle: Distributed Event-Triggered Nash Equilibrium Seeking Under Hybrid Attacks and Dead-Zone Inputs: A Topology Reconstruction Approach
abstract: A distributed Nash equilibrium (NE) seeking algorithm is proposed for multi-agent systems under non-cooperative game settings, where players are subject to hybrid attacks composed of Denial-of-service (DoS) and false data injection (FDI) attacks. The unknown dead-zone inputs are also taken into account for each agent. An event-triggered strategy is employed to enhance communication efficiency. With a topology reconstruction scheme, the impacts of hybrid attacks are mitigated. With the proposed event-triggered NE-seeking algorithm, the convergence of the distributed NE-seeking algorithm is analyzed, and an upper bound for the DoS attack time ratio is provided. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Handling Stability Hierarchical Control of Distributed Drive Electric Vehicle Based on Adaptive Dynamic Programming
abstract: In this paper, a hierarchical torque control strategy is presented that aims to improve the yaw stability of electric vehicles with distributed propulsion by using adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) under multiple constraints. First, the problem of yaw stability in the upper layer is reformulated as an optimisation problem. An ADP algorithm is employed to compute the optimal additional yaw moment. Constraints related to driving force, additional yaw moment and actuator limitations are considered in the lower layer. Optimum distribution of torque to the four wheels is then achieved using a quadratic programming algorithm to ensure stable vehicle handling. Finally, joint simulations using Carsim and Simulink are used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. The system's handling stability is assessed under steering-wheel angle step input conditions and during a snake test, in accordance with international standards.

articleTitle: Stability Criteria for Neural Networks with Stochastic Impulsive Intensity and Impulsive Density
abstract: This paper studies stability conditions for neural networks with stochastic impulsive intensity and impulsive density. Firstly, the pth moment exponential stability conditions are given, where the impulsive intensities of impulsive neural networks are independent and identically distributed, and the impulsive sequence is defined by impulsive density. Then, taking a linear time-varying impulsive system as an example, it is shown that impulsive sequence defined by average impulsive interval is sometime insufficient in terms of stabilizing such linear time-varying systems. Finally, two examples are presented to verify that impulsive density method is more effective and universal than average impulsive interval method when dealing with time-varying systems.
